decisions.reason: As a classic door lever handle, it is very close to the firm's existing metalworking and door-hardware knowledge, so the firm can readily interpret early feedback and improve it rather than withdraw it quickly.

A door lever handle family builds directly on established product architecture and production capabilities, making it a low-risk extension that a large German manufacturer would usually retain to deepen its range.
Although a new door handle design may face some market-selection risk, it still relies on familiar materials, manufacturing and customer knowledge, which supports continued learning and refinement.

This design variant is related enough to the firm's core competences to justify continued commercialization, though design-led products are somewhat more exposed to rapid portfolio pruning if demand is weak.
Another door lever handle family fits strongly within the firm's absorptive base and can share tooling, sales channels and know-how, so it is unlikely to be removed after only a short market test.

The electronic access system is more knowledge-distant than the mechanical handle products, but its adjacency to the firm's access hardware business and the firm's scale make continued development and learning more likely than an early exit.
